question.leadin: The term "Deluge" refers to a period in which Sweden occupied a union of these two countries, which was governed by a parliament called the sejm (same).
question.text: Name these two countries that signed the 1569 Union of Lublin, unifying into a commonwealth that would last until it lost its land in a series of 18th century partitions.
question.answerHtml: Poland and Lithuania [or the Kingdom of Poland and the Grand Duchy of Lithuania, or Korona Królestwa Polskiego and Didi Kunigystė Lietuvos or the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth]
question.clue: The head of one of these countries instigated Zeligowski's Mutiny in the other.

swap.leadin: A radio mast in this city was the tallest manmade structure in the world prior to its collapse in 1991.
swap.text: Name this capital city on the Vistula River. The most famous anti-Nazi Jewish uprising occurred in this city's ghetto, where the Muranow neighborhood was built after the war using "rubble-concrete" from the destroyed buildings.
swap.clue: This city was where Chancellor Willy Brandt appeared to spontaneously kneel in December 1970.

question.leadin: Any member of this political body would immediate dissolve it with the words "I do not allow," the Liberum veto. --.
question.text: Name this parliamentary body of an eastern European "commonwealth."
question.clue: The szlachta class composed the majority of its Chamber of Deputies.

swap.leadin: It was partitioned several times in the late 18th century.
swap.text: Name this region whose king Jan Sobieski III dispersed the Ottomans during the Second Siege of Vienna, which became a modern-day country with its capital at Warsaw.
swap.clue: Rulers of this kingdom agreed to a set of "articles" named after Henry of Valois, its first elected king.

question.leadin: Answer the following about figures in the Scientific Revolution.
question.text: The Scientific Revolution is often said to have begun with the publication of On the Revolutions of Heavenly Spheres by this astronomer and proponent of heliocentrism.
question.clue: In his most famous work, which he dedicated to Pope Paul III, he preserved the concept of "epicycles" and attempted to explain patterns of retrograde motion.

swap.leadin: This largest Polish trade union emerged from the Lenin Shipyards.
swap.text: Name this trade union formed in the socialist state of Poland that became the name of a social movement against communist ideology in the Eastern Bloc.
swap.clue: It rose directly out of the KOR, while its rural branch was led by Jan Kulaj.

question.text: This adorable bear was purchased by Polish soldiers during World War II, being taught to move artillery and apparently enjoying eating cigarettes. His name is a diminutive for "joyful warrior."
question.clue: This Syrian Brown Bear who fought with the Polish II Corps and famously carried 100 pound cases of artillery across the battlefield.

swap.text: In spring 1940, Stalin approved a mass execution at this site, at which about 22,000 Polish nationals and prisoners of war were killed by the Soviet NKVD.

question.text: Algirdas's victory over the Golden Horde at the Battle of Blue Waters drove the greatest expansionary period of this polity, whose ruler Vytautus's involvement with the Samogitian uprisings and incessant warring with the Teutonic Knights helped prompt the Battle of Grunwald. For 15 points, identify this Grand Duchy which participated in the 1569 Union of Lublin.
question.clue: This country which joined with its western neighbor in the 1569 Union of Lublin. In the 20th century, this Baltic state was the first to declare its independence from the Soviet Union.

swap.text: Jogaila was the Grand Duke of what became this Baltic nation with a capital at Vilnius.
swap.clue: Another Grand Duke of this nation signed the Union of Krewo to marry Jadwiga of Anjou.

question.text: Walesa attended one version of these negotiations that occurred in several countries between the Communist regimes and the opposition. In Poland in 1989, these talks resulted in semi-free elections and a victory for Solidarity.
question.clue: After the picnic, democracy came about through one of these orderly discussions in 1989. The Hungarian version of these events were inspired by ones organized by Solidarity in Poland.

swap.leadin: This man represented opposition groups at the Round Table Talks.
swap.text: Name this electrician who led the trade union Solidarity.
swap.clue: The KOR ("K-O-R") was a predecessor to an organization led by this man, which formed a coalition government with the PUWP.

question.leadin: A "general crisis" named for this century led to a population decline in Europe and possibly other parts of the world.
question.text: Name this century, in which both the Thirty Years' War and the Dutch Golden Age ended.
question.clue: 27 Czech leaders were executed in Prague's Old Town Square during this century, partially as revenge for an earlier event in which Ferdinand II's Catholic representatives were hurled out a window.

swap.text: This king was victorious over the Ottomans at Chocim and at the Battle of the Kahlenberg, lifting the siege of Vienna in 1683, making him surely the most pivotal ruler from the house of Sobieski.
swap.answerHtml: Jan III Sobieski (or John III, prompt on Jan)
swap.clue: His victory at Chocim coincided with the death of his predecessor Michael I, allowing him to take power.

question.leadin: This house lost power after the death of Casimir III the Great, the son of Wladyslaw the Elbow-High.
question.text: Name this dynasty founded by Mieszko I that ruled an oft-partitioned country in eastern Europe.

swap.leadin: This king equipped the Winged Hussars with lances for the first time and transformed them from light cavalry to an elite shock force.
swap.text: Name this Polish king who reigned with his wife, Anna Jagiellon ("yag-YELL-on"). This monarch concluded the Peace of Jam Zapolski with Ivan the Terrible after besieging Pskov ("pss-KOFF") during the Livonian War.
swap.clue: This leader's military reforms led to the adoption of the kopia by his country's cavalry and he curtailed the rights of the city of Danzig when it rebelled against him after his victory in an election over Maximilian II.

question.leadin: The Peace of Thorn followed this victory for Vytautas the Great and Jogaila, also known as Wladyslaw II Jagiello, against Grand Master Ulrich von Jungingen.
question.text: Name this 1410 battle, in which Poland and Lithuania decisively defeated the Teutonic Order. It shares one of its alternate names with a key battle of World War I's eastern front.
question.clue: The Peace of Thorn showed the failure of the winning side to capitalize on this victory.

swap.text: Sobieski came to the throne at the end of this chaotic period in Polish history. It began roughly with the Khmelnytsky Uprising and included an invasion of the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth by Sweden.
swap.clue: D.C. Stephenson's trial almost destroyed this organization, and it and The ADL arose after the lynching of Leo Frank in Atlanta.

question.leadin: This man argued that it is "better to have a friend than a slave" in his seminal Essay on Diplomacy, which he wrote under the pseudonym "Philhellene" ("feel-eh-LEN").
question.text: Name this man who founded the Historical and Literary Society in Paris. This man bought the Hotel Lambert, which lends its name to a faction of people led by this man that participated in the Great Emigration.

swap.leadin: Eric Hobsbawm characterized the start of this period as a "major servile upheaval" during the 17th-century "General Crisis."
swap.text: Give this term for the chaotic period after the Khmelnytsky Uprising in Ukraine, when the Hetmanate's Left and Right Banks were divided. It overlapped with the Polish-Lithuanian Deluge.
